Reddit is popular, but seems to be dying. Voat seems to be the next site in the cycle.

I'm a huge linguistics nerd, and I love incorporating that into worldbuilding. Does anyone here have alternate languages for their worlds besides English? If not, I hope to convince you to incorporate one here! One of the best things about having a unique language set to your world is that it can be custom designed to reflect the culture of its origin. I would love to hear about any languages made unique to your world and how they are used to make it more vibrant.

I haven't fully created one, but took a linguistics class last year and it got me thinking about a culture that uses the unvoiced/voiced dichotomy in words to actually reveal something about the nature of the word itself. For example, if the word for hill was "kinto," ("kin-" or "ki-" meaning earth and "to-" meaning air), the word for mountain would be "gindo." Emotions could work similarly: the word for like could be something like "pasa" while the word for love could be something like "baza."

Anyone who is more into linguistics than me, could they give me any tips or ideas that might help me develop this further?
I would love to help but your question seems very vague to me. You seem to be off to a solid start, what kind of tips are you looking for?
I guess just a guide on building a language. Sorry for the vagueness.. I just don't know where to start!

http://www.zompist.com/kit.html is the link the other user posted here, which looks to be a very strong starting point. Aside from that I would say it really depends on how detailed you want to get with it. Are you looking into doing a full conlang kind of thing? Or would some basic grammar and vocab be sufficient? Keep in mind that it isn't too hard to use some of the basics to imply that there is a lot more to the language, even if it isn't necessarily all fleshed out.

I'm so glad to see this, I always wished the conlang and worldbuilding subs workedd together more over on that other place.

I'm in the process of designing the first two languages from which all others are derived. It's very fun designing a language that is rudimentary and simple, since I can do it without needing to really hit the books on linguistics.
How do i start to create a language? For example a colony of hunters and gatherers, a not so developed group of people. What would be the basic steps?

http://www.zompist.com/kit.html

I've been interested in conlanging before, and whenever I asked for help, this website is what I was given.

There's also /v/conlangs, or if you're willing to still use Reddit, there's also /r/conlangs, which has more users and activity.

The link the other guy posted it a good resource. I don't think it is necessary for worldbuilding to go into full on conlanging unless you really want to. Start out with some basic verbs and nouns and add more as needed for the sake of depth. Think about the culture in your world and what it values, and how those values might be reflected in the language they speak.
